argument_summary: The strongest admissible defense is narrow: current evidence supports overall operational readiness because the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.1 percentage points and the launch rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents. Public governance guidance also supports deployment decisions grounded in documented evaluation results, limitations, and ongoing risk management. That said, the same admissible record shows a current loan-modification-support regression 1.4 percentage points below the warning threshold and no attached approved mitigation, risk acceptance, or disclosure language for that named use case. The certification case is therefore supportable only as a weak, limited governance judgment, not as a clean showing that every policy predicate is fully satisfied.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position, and none is offered as a basis to relax the policy standard.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit treating prior approval or an informal monitoring note as a substitute for current-release evidence. The prior approval is contextual only because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch. The informal monitoring comment is also contextual only because the record does not show reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language. The admissible policy-consistent position is therefore that aggregate readiness supports certification on a narrow operational basis, while the unresolved subgroup weakness prevents any claim of fully clean compliance.
concessions: The current record does not support a claim of fully clean compliance.
The loan modification support slice is a current named-use-case weakness and sits 1.4 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The record does not include approved pre-launch risk acceptance, reviewed mitigation, or attached disclosure language for that weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family cannot satisfy the current-release evidence requirement.
